128	## Step 4: Classifiers (`src/models.py`)
129	
130	**Approach.** Three scikit-learn models, all `random_state=42`, trained on the preprocessed 2014-2016 data.
131	
132	**Functions.**
133	- `build_model(name: str) -> sklearn estimator`: `name` in `{"logreg", "random_forest", "sgd"}`; raises `ValueError` otherwise.
134	- `train_model(name: str, X_train: np.ndarray, y_train: np.ndarray) -> estimator`: builds and fits.
135	- `train_all(X_train, y_train) -> dict[str, estimator]`.
136	- `train_all_from_split(split: dict) -> dict[str, estimator]`: the static Step 4 entry point; wraps `train_all` and raises if `set(split["years_train"]) <= set(TRAIN_YEARS)` is false. This guard is for the static 2014-2016 model only; Step 7 windows (2017+) do not use it. Step 7 uses `window_years` plus `check_no_overlap` instead (see Step 7).
137	- `tune_logreg(tune_split: dict) -> dict`: only if time allows: small grid on `C` using train 2014-2015 / validate 2016, scoring F1 (malware); returns best params and the grid scores.
138	- `MODEL_NAMES: tuple[str, ...]`.
139	
140	**Models and hyperparameter justification.**
141	- `LogisticRegression(class_weight="balanced", max_iter=1000, solver="lbfgs", C=1.0, random_state=42)`: linear baseline that works well on scaled sparse-ish counts; `balanced` protects against label imbalance if present (the data is balanced per year, but later use may not be); `max_iter=1000` so lbfgs converges on ~1,000 standardized features (a `ConvergenceWarning` is treated as a problem to report); `C=1.0` is the default, changed only if tuning on 2016 says so.
142	- `RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, n_jobs=-1, random_state=42)`: non-linear model that is insensitive to feature scale; 200 trees is a point where accuracy usually plateaus while training stays within a minute or two on ~54,000 rows; other settings default (unbounded depth, `max_features="sqrt"`).

For `partial_fit` the first call passes `classes=[0, 1]`.

174	## Step 7: Sustainable approach (`src/sustainable.py`)
175	
176	**Approach.** Compare four strategies on the same test years (2017-2021), same metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, F1; malware positive), reported per year and pooled. Rule for all of them: year t is predicted before any of its rows is used for training or for fitting preprocessing.
177	
178	| Strategy | Training data used to predict year t |
179	|---|---|
180	| (a) static | 2014-2016 only, never updated (this is the Step 4/6 model) |
181	| (b) expanding window | all years before t (2014..t-1); preprocessing and model refit from scratch for each t |
182	| (c) sliding window | the 3 years before t (t-3..t-1); preprocessing and model refit for each t |
183	| (d) incremental | SGD fit on 2014-2016, then for t = 2017..2021: predict t, then `partial_fit` on t (test-then-train) |
184	
185	For t=2017 the windows in (b) and (c) are both 2014-2016, so (a)-(c) agree on 2017; they differ from 2018 on.
186	
187	**Functions.**
188	- Step 7 guard: every Step 7 fit goes through `window_years` (which raises if any returned year is >= t) and then `check_no_overlap(window, [t])`. `train_all_from_split` is not used here.
189	- `window_years(strategy: str, t: int) -> tuple[int, ...]`: training years for strategy `"static"`, `"expanding"` or `"sliding"` at test year t (static: 2014-2016; expanding: 2014..t-1; sliding: t-3..t-1); raises if t is not in `TEST_YEARS` or if any returned year is >= t.
190	- `run_window_strategy(df, strategy: str, model_name: str = "logreg") -> pd.DataFrame`: for each t: `check_no_overlap(window, [t])`, fit a new `Preprocessor` and model on the window only, predict t, compute metrics; returns one row per test year.
191	- `run_incremental(df, model_name: str = "sgd") -> pd.DataFrame`: initial `fit` of `Preprocessor` and SGD on 2014-2016 (preprocessor frozen afterwards, so later years use the same mask and scaler: a limitation noted in the report); loop over t, record the prediction on t first, then `partial_fit` on year t with the true labels. Returns one row per test year.
192	- `run_all_strategies(df, split=None, models=None, step4_seconds=None, rf=True) -> pd.DataFrame`: concatenates (a)-(d) with `strategy` and `classifier` columns, one row per (strategy, classifier, test year); static rows come from the Step 4 models when given. **Changed in Step 7:** the pooled rows are not in this table (a `year` column stays numeric); `pooled_by_strategy` writes them separately.
193	- `compare_to_static(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame`: per strategy and year, difference in F1 and accuracy against the static model.
194	- `run_sustainable(df, split=None, models=None, step4_seconds=None, rf=True) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]`: writes `results/step7_strategies.*` (columns `strategy, classifier, year, n, accuracy, precision, recall, f1`; replaces the planned name `step7_strategy_metrics`, as the lead engineer asked), `step7_strategies_detail.*` (adds confusion counts, training seconds, rows and window), `step7_pooled.*`, `step7_vs_static.*`, `step7_summary.*` (mean F1, worst year), `step7_cost.*`, `step7_window_composition.*` and `step7_f1_by_year.png` (F1 and accuracy by year, dashed always-malware F1 0.667 and chance accuracy 0.5).
195	- Helpers: `year_arrays`, `fit_on_years` (the single place every window fit goes through: `check_no_overlap` plus a `max(years) < t` assertion), `static_from_models`, `pooled_by_strategy`, `summary_table`, `cost_table`, `window_composition`, `plot_strategies`. `run_incremental` also asserts before every prediction that no year seen so far is >= t.
196	
197	**Model choice and decision flagged.** Windows (b)-(c) and the static baseline use LogisticRegression so that all five refits finish in a few minutes; (d) uses SGD. A fair isolation of "incremental vs retrain" would also run SGD under (a)-(c); I will add SGD-static as an extra row (cheap) so the incremental gain is compared with the same model family. RandomForest is run for (a) and (b) only (not (c) or (d)); measured, it fit within the budget. Runtime estimate: ~54,000-90,000 rows x ~1,000 features per LR refit, 5 refits per strategy; to be measured, not assumed.
198	
199	**Assumption to state.** Labels for year t become available only after year t ends (test-then-train); a real labeling delay would hurt (d), (b) and (c) in practice. The report states this. Not simulated here.
200	
201	**Row-count imbalance (to state in the report).** Years 2014-2018 have 18,000 rows each and 2019-2021 have 3,000, so the expanding window is dominated by old data and the 3-year window for 2021 (2018-2020) is 18,000 of 24,000 rows from 2018. The report notes that "retraining helps or not" may partly reflect this row-count imbalance rather than recency alone, and lists each window's year composition (rows per year in the training window for every strategy and test year; also saved as `results/step7_window_composition.csv`). No equal-rows variant is run.
202	
203	**Report.** `docs/step7_sustainable_approach.md`: the four strategies, the table of F1/accuracy per year, the window composition table and the imbalance note above, comparison with the static model, cost (training time per strategy), conclusions that feed the one-page report.
204	
205	**Testing.** Synthetic multi-year frame with an injected drift (class boundary shifts each year): `window_years` returns exactly the specified years (including edge cases t=2017 and t=2021); for every strategy and every t, `max(window) < t` (the no-test-year-in-training check, run through a spy that records the years passed to `fit`); `run_incremental` records predictions on t before `partial_fit` on t (verified with a stub model that logs call order and, separately, by checking the year-t labels are not seen at prediction time); static results are identical to the Step 6 model's results; result tables have one row per test year per strategy and the expected columns; on the injected-drift data the retraining/incremental strategies do not do worse than the static one in the final year (sanity check, not a performance claim).
206

215	One commit per task (about 300 added lines max): config + data, then drift, then preprocess, then models, then evaluate, then sustainable, then main and docs. Each step is followed by a review and test cycle outside this plan.

218	1. The accuracy matrix in Step 2 trains on later years and predicts earlier ones; this is a diagnostic only, not used for any design choice, and is exempt from the leakage rules (section 0).

1	"""Step 7: sustainable approaches (static, expanding window, sliding window, incremental) on test years 2017-2021.
2	
3	Rule for every strategy: year t is predicted before any of its rows is used to fit preprocessing or a model.
4	"""
5	from __future__ import annotations
6	
7	import time
8	import warnings
9	from pathlib import Path
10	from typing import Any
11	
12	import numpy as np
13	import pandas as pd
14	from sklearn.exceptions import ConvergenceWarning
15	
16	from src.config import LABEL_COL, RESULTS_DIR, TEST_YEARS, TRAIN_YEARS, YEAR_COL
17	from src.data import feature_columns
18	from src.evaluate import compute_metrics, confusion_counts, save_table
19	from src.models import train_model
20	from src.preprocess import Preprocessor, check_no_overlap
21	
22	STRATEGIES: tuple[str, ...] = ("static", "expanding", "sliding", "incremental")
23	WINDOW_SIZE: int = 3  # sliding window: the 3 years before the test year
24	EXPORT_COLUMNS: list[str] = ["strategy", "classifier", "year", "n", "accuracy", "precision", "recall", "f1"]
25	YearArrays = dict[int, tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]
26	
27	
28	def window_years(strategy: str, t: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
29	    """Training years for `strategy` ("static", "expanding", "sliding") when predicting test year t.
30	
31	    static: 2014-2016; expanding: 2014..t-1; sliding: t-3..t-1. Raises ValueError if t is not a test year, the
32	    strategy is unknown, or any returned year is >= t (the leakage guard shared by every Step 7 fit).
33	    """
34	    if t not in TEST_YEARS:
35	        raise ValueError(f"t={t} is not a test year {TEST_YEARS}")
36	    if strategy == "static":
37	        years = tuple(TRAIN_YEARS)
38	    elif strategy == "expanding":
39	        years = tuple(range(min(TRAIN_YEARS), t))
40	    elif strategy == "sliding":
41	        years = tuple(range(t - WINDOW_SIZE, t))
42	    else:
43	        raise ValueError(f"unknown window strategy {strategy!r}; expected static, expanding or sliding")
44	    if not years or max(years) >= t:
45	        raise ValueError(f"window {years} for {strategy} must be non-empty and precede test year {t}")
46	    return years
47	
48	
49	def year_arrays(df: pd.DataFrame) -> YearArrays:
50	    """Raw float32 feature matrix and labels per year, extracted once so windows only concatenate."""
51	    features = feature_columns(df)
52	    out: YearArrays = {}
53	    for year, g in df.groupby(YEAR_COL, sort=True):
54	        out[int(year)] = (g[features].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32), g[LABEL_COL].to_numpy())
55	    return out
56	
57	
58	def _stack(arrays: YearArrays, years: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
59	    """Concatenate the raw rows and labels of `years` (in the order given)."""
60	    return np.concatenate([arrays[y][0] for y in years]), np.concatenate([arrays[y][1] for y in years])
61	
62	
63	def fit_on_years(
64	    arrays: YearArrays, features: list[str], years: tuple[int, ...], t: int, model_name: str
65	) -> tuple[Preprocessor, Any, float, int, int]:
66	    """Fit a new Preprocessor and model on `years` only, after checking they all precede test year t.
67	
68	    Every window fit goes through here (tests spy on it). Returns (preprocessor, model, seconds,
69	    n_training_rows, convergence_warnings); seconds covers preprocessing plus model fit.
70	    """
71	    check_no_overlap(years, [t])
72	    if max(years) >= t:  # belt and braces: check_no_overlap already enforces this
73	        raise AssertionError(f"training years {years} include a year >= {t}")
74	    X_raw, y = _stack(arrays, years)
75	    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
76	        warnings.simplefilter("always")
77	        start = time.perf_counter()
78	        pre = Preprocessor().fit(X_raw, features)  # window rows only
79	        model = train_model(model_name, pre.transform(X_raw), y)
80	        seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
81	    n_conv = sum(issubclass(w.category, ConvergenceWarning) for w in caught)
82	    return pre, model, seconds, len(y), n_conv
83	
84	
85	def _result_row(
86	    strategy: str, classifier: str, t: int, y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray,
87	    seconds: float, train_rows: int, years: tuple[int, ...], n_conv: int = 0,
88	) -> dict[str, Any]:
89	    """One result row: metrics, confusion counts, cost and the training window for one (strategy, classifier, year)."""
90	    return {"strategy": strategy, "classifier": classifier, "year": t, "n": len(y_true),
91	            **compute_metrics(y_true, y_pred), **confusion_counts(y_true, y_pred),
92	            "train_seconds": seconds, "train_rows": train_rows, "window": f"{min(years)}-{max(years)}",
93	            "convergence_warnings": n_conv}
94	
95	
96	def run_window_strategy(
97	    df: pd.DataFrame, strategy: str, model_name: str = "logreg", arrays: YearArrays | None = None
98	) -> pd.DataFrame:
99	    """Static, expanding or sliding strategy: for each test year t, fit on its window only, predict t.
100	
101	    The static window is the same for every t, so it is fitted once (same result as refitting five times).
102	    Returns one row per test year.
103	    """
104	    arrays = year_arrays(df) if arrays is None else arrays
105	    features = feature_columns(df)
106	    rows, fitted = [], {}
107	    for t in TEST_YEARS:
108	        years = window_years(strategy, t)  # raises if any year >= t
109	        if strategy != "static" or years not in fitted:
110	            fitted[years] = fit_on_years(arrays, features, years, t, model_name)
111	        pre, model, seconds, n_rows, n_conv = fitted[years]
112	        X_t, y_t = arrays[t]
113	        pred = model.predict(pre.transform(X_t))  # year t is only transformed/predicted here
114	        # Static cost is paid once (first test year); later rows record 0 retraining seconds.
115	        paid = seconds if (strategy != "static" or t == TEST_YEARS[0]) else 0.0
116	        rows.append(_result_row(strategy, model_name, t, y_t, pred, paid, n_rows, years, n_conv))
117	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
118	
119	
120	def run_incremental(df: pd.DataFrame, model_name: str = "sgd", arrays: YearArrays | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
121	    """Incremental test-then-train: fit on 2014-2016, then for each t predict t and only afterwards `partial_fit` on t.
122	
123	    The preprocessor (zero-column mask, scaler) is fitted on 2014-2016 and frozen, so year t never influences it.
124	    train_seconds of a row is the cost of the update that produced the model used for that row's prediction
125	    (2017: the initial fit; later years: the partial_fit on the previous year).
126	    """
127	    arrays = year_arrays(df) if arrays is None else arrays
128	    features = feature_columns(df)
129	    pre, model, seconds, n_rows, n_conv = fit_on_years(arrays, features, tuple(TRAIN_YEARS), TEST_YEARS[0], model_name)
130	    seen = list(TRAIN_YEARS)
131	    rows = []
132	    for t in TEST_YEARS:
133	        if max(seen) >= t:  # every year used so far must precede the year being predicted
134	            raise AssertionError(f"incremental model has seen {seen}, which includes a year >= {t}")
135	        X_t, y_t = arrays[t]
136	        Z_t = pre.transform(X_t)  # frozen preprocessor: transform only
137	        pred = model.predict(Z_t)  # 1) predict t ...
138	        rows.append(_result_row("incremental", model_name, t, y_t, pred, seconds, n_rows, tuple(seen), n_conv))
139	        start = time.perf_counter()
140	        model.partial_fit(Z_t, y_t)  # 2) ... then learn from t (labels arrive after the year ends)
141	        seconds, n_rows, n_conv = time.perf_counter() - start, len(y_t), 0
142	        seen.append(t)
143	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
144

146	def static_from_models(split: dict, models: dict[str, Any], train_seconds: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
147	    """Static rows from the already fitted Step 4 models (nothing is refitted). train_seconds: Step 4 fit times."""
148	    rows = []
149	    years_train = tuple(sorted(set(split["years_train"].tolist())))
150	    for name, model in models.items():
151	        pred = model.predict(split["X_test"])
152	        for t in TEST_YEARS:
153	            sel = split["years_test"] == t
154	            secs = (train_seconds or {}).get(name, float("nan")) if t == TEST_YEARS[0] else 0.0
155	            rows.append(_result_row("static", name, t, split["y_test"][sel], pred[sel], secs, len(split["y_train"]), years_train))
156	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

158	
159	def run_all_strategies(
160	    df: pd.DataFrame,
161	    split: dict | None = None,
162	    models: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
163	    step4_seconds: dict[str, float] | None = None,
164	    rf: bool = True,
165	) -> pd.DataFrame:
166	    """Run (a)-(d) for logreg and SGD, plus static and expanding for random forest (rf=True).

"""Step 7: sustainable approaches (static, expanding window, sliding window, incremental) on test years 2017-2021.

Rule for every strategy: year t is predicted before any of its rows is used to fit preprocessing or a model.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import time
import warnings
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.exceptions import ConvergenceWarning

from src.config import LABEL_COL, RESULTS_DIR, TEST_YEARS, TRAIN_YEARS, YEAR_COL
from src.data import feature_columns
from src.evaluate import compute_metrics, confusion_counts, save_table
from src.models import train_model
from src.preprocess import Preprocessor, check_no_overlap

STRATEGIES: tuple[str, ...] = ("static", "expanding", "sliding", "incremental")
WINDOW_SIZE: int = 3  # sliding window: the 3 years before the test year
EXPORT_COLUMNS: list[str] = ["strategy", "classifier", "year", "n", "accuracy", "precision", "recall", "f1"]
YearArrays = dict[int, tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]


def window_years(strategy: str, t: int) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """Training years for `strategy` ("static", "expanding", "sliding") when predicting test year t.

    static: 2014-2016; expanding: 2014..t-1; sliding: t-3..t-1. Raises ValueError if t is not a test year, the
    strategy is unknown, or any returned year is >= t (the leakage guard shared by every Step 7 fit).
    """
    if t not in TEST_YEARS:
        raise ValueError(f"t={t} is not a test year {TEST_YEARS}")
    if strategy == "static":
        years = tuple(TRAIN_YEARS)
    elif strategy == "expanding":
        years = tuple(range(min(TRAIN_YEARS), t))
    elif strategy == "sliding":
        years = tuple(range(t - WINDOW_SIZE, t))
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown window strategy {strategy!r}; expected static, expanding or sliding")
    if not years or max(years) >= t:
        raise ValueError(f"window {years} for {strategy} must be non-empty and precede test year {t}")
    return years


def year_arrays(df: pd.DataFrame) -> YearArrays:
    """Raw float32 feature matrix and labels per year, extracted once so windows only concatenate."""
    features = feature_columns(df)
    out: YearArrays = {}
    for year, g in df.groupby(YEAR_COL, sort=True):
        out[int(year)] = (g[features].to_numpy(dtype=np.float32), g[LABEL_COL].to_numpy())
    return out


def _stack(arrays: YearArrays, years: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Concatenate the raw rows and labels of `years` (in the order given)."""
    return np.concatenate([arrays[y][0] for y in years]), np.concatenate([arrays[y][1] for y in years])


def fit_on_years(
    arrays: YearArrays, features: list[str], years: tuple[int, ...], t: int, model_name: str
) -> tuple[Preprocessor, Any, float, int, int]:
    """Fit a new Preprocessor and model on `years` only, after checking they all precede test year t.

    Every window fit goes through here (tests spy on it). Returns (preprocessor, model, seconds,
    n_training_rows, convergence_warnings); seconds covers preprocessing plus model fit.
    """
    check_no_overlap(years, [t])
    if max(years) >= t:  # belt and braces: check_no_overlap already enforces this
        raise AssertionError(f"training years {years} include a year >= {t}")
    X_raw, y = _stack(arrays, years)
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        start = time.perf_counter()
        pre = Preprocessor().fit(X_raw, features)  # window rows only
        model = train_model(model_name, pre.transform(X_raw), y)
        seconds = time.perf_counter() - start
    n_conv = sum(issubclass(w.category, ConvergenceWarning) for w in caught)
    return pre, model, seconds, len(y), n_conv


def _result_row(
    strategy: str, classifier: str, t: int, y_true: np.ndarray, y_pred: np.ndarray,
    seconds: float, train_rows: int, years: tuple[int, ...], n_conv: int = 0,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """One result row: metrics, confusion counts, cost and the training window for one (strategy, classifier, year)."""
    return {"strategy": strategy, "classifier": classifier, "year": t, "n": len(y_true),
            **compute_metrics(y_true, y_pred), **confusion_counts(y_true, y_pred),
            "train_seconds": seconds, "train_rows": train_rows, "window": f"{min(years)}-{max(years)}",
            "convergence_warnings": n_conv}


def run_window_strategy(
    df: pd.DataFrame, strategy: str, model_name: str = "logreg", arrays: YearArrays | None = None
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Static, expanding or sliding strategy: for each test year t, fit on its window only, predict t.

    The static window is the same for every t, so it is fitted once (same result as refitting five times).
    Returns one row per test year.
    """
    arrays = year_arrays(df) if arrays is None else arrays
    features = feature_columns(df)
    rows, fitted = [], {}
    for t in TEST_YEARS:
        years = window_years(strategy, t)  # raises if any year >= t
        if strategy != "static" or years not in fitted:
            fitted[years] = fit_on_years(arrays, features, years, t, model_name)
        pre, model, seconds, n_rows, n_conv = fitted[years]
        X_t, y_t = arrays[t]
        pred = model.predict(pre.transform(X_t))  # year t is only transformed/predicted here
        # Static cost is paid once (first test year); later rows record 0 retraining seconds.
        paid = seconds if (strategy != "static" or t == TEST_YEARS[0]) else 0.0
        rows.append(_result_row(strategy, model_name, t, y_t, pred, paid, n_rows, years, n_conv))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def run_incremental(df: pd.DataFrame, model_name: str = "sgd", arrays: YearArrays | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Incremental test-then-train: fit on 2014-2016, then for each t predict t and only afterwards `partial_fit` on t.

    The preprocessor (zero-column mask, scaler) is fitted on 2014-2016 and frozen, so year t never influences it.
    train_seconds of a row is the cost of the update that produced the model used for that row's prediction
    (2017: the initial fit; later years: the partial_fit on the previous year).
    """
    arrays = year_arrays(df) if arrays is None else arrays
    features = feature_columns(df)
    pre, model, seconds, n_rows, n_conv = fit_on_years(arrays, features, tuple(TRAIN_YEARS), TEST_YEARS[0], model_name)
    seen = list(TRAIN_YEARS)
    rows = []
    for t in TEST_YEARS:
        if max(seen) >= t:  # every year used so far must precede the year being predicted
            raise AssertionError(f"incremental model has seen {seen}, which includes a year >= {t}")
        X_t, y_t = arrays[t]
        Z_t = pre.transform(X_t)  # frozen preprocessor: transform only
        pred = model.predict(Z_t)  # 1) predict t ...
        rows.append(_result_row("incremental", model_name, t, y_t, pred, seconds, n_rows, tuple(seen), n_conv))
        start = time.perf_counter()
        model.partial_fit(Z_t, y_t)  # 2) ... then learn from t (labels arrive after the year ends)
        seconds, n_rows, n_conv = time.perf_counter() - start, len(y_t), 0
        seen.append(t)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def static_from_models(split: dict, models: dict[str, Any], train_seconds: dict[str, float] | None = None) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Static rows from the already fitted Step 4 models (nothing is refitted). train_seconds: Step 4 fit times."""
    rows = []
    years_train = tuple(sorted(set(split["years_train"].tolist())))
    for name, model in models.items():
        pred = model.predict(split["X_test"])
        for t in TEST_YEARS:
            sel = split["years_test"] == t
            secs = (train_seconds or {}).get(name, float("nan")) if t == TEST_YEARS[0] else 0.0
            rows.append(_result_row("static", name, t, split["y_test"][sel], pred[sel], secs, len(split["y_train"]), years_train))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def run_all_strategies(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    split: dict | None = None,
    models: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    step4_seconds: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    rf: bool = True,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Run (a)-(d) for logreg and SGD, plus static and expanding for random forest (rf=True).

    split/models: Step 4 split and fitted models; if both are given the static rows come from those models.
    Returns one row per (strategy, classifier, test year).
    """
    arrays = year_arrays(df)
    parts = []
    plan = {"logreg": ("static", "expanding", "sliding"), "sgd": ("static", "expanding", "sliding", "incremental")}
    if rf:
        plan["random_forest"] = ("static", "expanding")
    for name, strategies in plan.items():
        for strategy in strategies:
            if strategy == "static" and split is not None and models is not None and name in models:
                parts.append(static_from_models(split, {name: models[name]}, step4_seconds))
            elif strategy == "incremental":
                parts.append(run_incremental(df, name, arrays))
            else:
                parts.append(run_window_strategy(df, strategy, name, arrays))
    return pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)


def pooled_by_strategy(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Metrics pooled over all test years per (strategy, classifier), from the summed confusion counts.

    Years are weighted by size (2017-2018 have 6x the rows of 2019-2021), so the per-year table is the main view.
    """
    rows = []
    for (strategy, clf), g in results.groupby(["strategy", "classifier"], sort=False):
        tn, fp, fn, tp = (int(g[c].sum()) for c in ("tn", "fp", "fn", "tp"))
        n = tn + fp + fn + tp
        prec = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else 0.0
        rec = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0
        f1 = 2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec) if prec + rec else 0.0
        rows.append({"strategy": strategy, "classifier": clf, "n": n, "accuracy": (tp + tn) / n,
                     "precision": prec, "recall": rec, "f1": f1})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def compare_to_static(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per (strategy, classifier, year): F1 and accuracy minus the static model of the same classifier."""
    static = results[results["strategy"] == "static"].set_index(["classifier", "year"])
    out = results[["strategy", "classifier", "year", "f1", "accuracy"]].copy()
    key = list(zip(out["classifier"], out["year"]))
    out["f1_static"] = [static["f1"].get(k, np.nan) for k in key]
    out["accuracy_static"] = [static["accuracy"].get(k, np.nan) for k in key]
    out["f1_diff"] = out["f1"] - out["f1_static"]
    out["accuracy_diff"] = out["accuracy"] - out["accuracy_static"]
    return out[out["strategy"] != "static"].reset_index(drop=True)


def summary_table(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per (strategy, classifier): mean F1 over the 5 test years (unweighted), worst year, 2019-2021 means, gain over static."""
    rows = []
    for (strategy, clf), g in results.groupby(["strategy", "classifier"], sort=False):
        worst = g.loc[g["f1"].idxmin()]
        late = g[g["year"] >= 2019]
        rows.append({"strategy": strategy, "classifier": clf, "mean_f1": g["f1"].mean(), "worst_f1": worst["f1"],
                     "worst_year": int(worst["year"]), "mean_f1_2019_21": late["f1"].mean(),
                     "mean_accuracy_2019_21": late["accuracy"].mean(), "mean_accuracy": g["accuracy"].mean()})
    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    base = out[out["strategy"] == "static"].set_index("classifier")
    out["mean_f1_gain_vs_static"] = out["mean_f1"] - out["classifier"].map(base["mean_f1"])
    out["mean_acc_2019_21_gain_vs_static"] = out["mean_accuracy_2019_21"] - out["classifier"].map(base["mean_accuracy_2019_21"])
    return out


def cost_table(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Training cost per (strategy, classifier): number of fits/updates, total and mean seconds, mean training rows."""
    rows = []
    for (strategy, clf), g in results.groupby(["strategy", "classifier"], sort=False):
        if strategy == "static":
            secs = g["train_seconds"].iloc[:1]  # one fit, paid once
        else:
            secs = g["train_seconds"]
        rows.append({"strategy": strategy, "classifier": clf, "n_fits": len(secs), "total_seconds": secs.sum(),
                     "mean_seconds_per_update": secs.mean(), "max_seconds": secs.max(),
                     "mean_train_rows": g["train_rows"].mean()})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def window_composition(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Rows per year in the training data behind each prediction, for every strategy and test year.

    The incremental model has seen the same years as the expanding window (2014..t-1) but through the single
    pass of `partial_fit`; its preprocessor only ever saw 2014-2016.
    """
    counts = df.groupby(YEAR_COL).size()
    rows = []
    for strategy in STRATEGIES:
        for t in TEST_YEARS:
            years = window_years("expanding" if strategy == "incremental" else strategy, t)
            total = int(sum(counts[y] for y in years))
            row = {"strategy": strategy, "test_year": t, "window": f"{min(years)}-{max(years)}", "train_rows": total}
            row.update({f"n_{y}": int(counts[y]) if y in years else 0 for y in sorted(counts.index)})
            row["share_2014_2018"] = sum(int(counts[y]) for y in years if y <= 2018) / total
            row["share_last_year"] = int(counts[max(years)]) / total
            rows.append(row)
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)


def plot_strategies(results: pd.DataFrame, path: Path) -> None:
    """Save F1 (top) and accuracy (bottom) by test year, one panel per classifier, one line per strategy.

    Dashed lines: F1 of always predicting malware on a balanced year (2*0.5/(0.5+1) = 0.667) and accuracy 0.5.
    """
    import matplotlib

    matplotlib.use("Agg")
    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

    clfs = list(dict.fromkeys(results["classifier"]))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, len(clfs), figsize=(4.5 * len(clfs), 7), sharex=True, squeeze=False)
    for j, clf in enumerate(clfs):
        for i, (metric, chance, label) in enumerate((("f1", 2 / 3, "always-malware F1 = 0.667"), ("accuracy", 0.5, "chance accuracy = 0.5"))):
            ax = axes[i][j]
            for strategy, g in results[results["classifier"] == clf].groupby("strategy", sort=False):
                g = g.sort_values("year")
                ax.plot(g["year"], g[metric], marker="o", label=strategy)
            ax.axhline(chance, ls="--", color="gray", label=label)
            ax.set_title(f"{clf}: {metric} by test year")
            ax.set_xticks(list(TEST_YEARS))
            ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
            ax.legend(fontsize=7)
            if j == 0:
                ax.set_ylabel(f"{metric} (malware = positive class)")
        axes[1][j].set_xlabel("test year")
    fig.tight_layout()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=120)
    plt.close(fig)


def run_sustainable(
    df: pd.DataFrame,
    split: dict | None = None,
    models: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    step4_seconds: dict[str, float] | None = None,
    rf: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    """Run all strategies, write results/step7_* (strategies, pooled, vs_static, summary, cost, window_composition, png)."""
    results = run_all_strategies(df, split, models, step4_seconds, rf)
    tables = {
        "strategies": results,
        "pooled": pooled_by_strategy(results),

# Step 6 Test Log: Test Data Prediction

- Tester transcript: transcripts/29_2026-11-03_tester_step6.md

## Tests written (tester)

One row per test function. Row counts follow AGENTS.md (2014-2018: 9,000 per file, so 18,000 per year; 2019-2021: 1,500 per file, so 3,000 per year), not ASSIGNMENT.md. Entry point tested: main.run_step6 (PLAN.md), plus evaluate.per_year_table.

| Test | What it checks (from the assignment or plan) |
| --- | --- |
| test_one_row_per_test_year_per_classifier | 15 rows: logreg, random_forest, sgd x 2017-2021, no duplicate (model, year) pairs |
| test_all_metric_values_between_0_and_1 | accuracy, precision, recall, f1 all in [0,1], no NaN |
| test_per_year_n_sums_to_total_test_rows | per-year n adds up to the number of 2017-2021 rows for each classifier; each year's n = rows in that year |
| test_no_training_year_in_per_year_table | no 2014-2016 year in any returned table with a year column |
| test_step6_writes_expected_files | results/step6_by_year.csv has columns classifier, year, n, accuracy, precision, recall, f1 and 15 rows |
| test_step6_only_predicts_with_given_models | stub models raise on fit/partial_fit and Preprocessor.fit is patched to raise; run_step6 still works (predict only) |
| test_step6_does_not_refit_passed_models | a fitted LogisticRegression keeps identical coef_/intercept_ after run_step6 |
| test_per_year_metrics_hand_checked_two_years | hand-computed two-year example (2017: acc 0.6, P/R/F1 2/3; 2018: acc 0.75, P/R/F1 0 with zero_division) |
| test_per_year_metrics_match_sklearn | per-year metrics equal scikit-learn (pos_label=1) on the same rows |
| test_run_step6_matches_sklearn_on_same_rows | end to end: run_step6 per-year f1/accuracy equal sklearn on each model's own predictions |
| test_year_outside_test_range_is_rejected | years 2013, 2016, 2022 in the test rows raise ValueError |
| test_single_class_test_year_does_not_crash | all-malware 2019 and all-benign 2021: 15 rows, no NaN, metrics in [0,1]; 2021 precision/recall/F1 = 0 |
| test_missing_test_year_is_not_invented | data without 2019: step raises, or table has exactly 2017, 2018, 2020, 2021 and no fake 2019 row |
| test_real_data_each_test_year_has_expected_rows | real data (skipped if absent): 18,000 rows for 2017-2018, 3,000 for 2019-2021; per-year n and metric range with a stub model (no retraining) |

## Failures and decisions (student)

One row per failing test. Decision is "Accepted" (the test is right; the builder fixes the code) or "Rejected" (the test is wrong; the tester fixes the test). Add the commit with the fix.

| Test | Cause | Decision | Fixed in commit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| test_step6_only_predicts_with_given_models | The test stub asserted that predict always sees all 600 test rows, but run_step6 also predicts on the smaller no-duplicate subset (552 rows), so it failed with 552 == 600. The code is right and the test setup was wrong; the tester fixed the stub and Run 2 passed. | Rejected | dc006ad |

187	def pooled_by_strategy(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
188	    """Metrics pooled over all test years per (strategy, classifier), from the summed confusion counts.
189	
190	    Years are weighted by size (2017-2018 have 6x the rows of 2019-2021), so the per-year table is the main view.
191	    """
192	    rows = []
193	    for (strategy, clf), g in results.groupby(["strategy", "classifier"], sort=False):
194	        tn, fp, fn, tp = (int(g[c].sum()) for c in ("tn", "fp", "fn", "tp"))
195	        n = tn + fp + fn + tp
196	        prec = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else 0.0
197	        rec = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0
198	        f1 = 2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec) if prec + rec else 0.0
199	        rows.append({"strategy": strategy, "classifier": clf, "n": n, "accuracy": (tp + tn) / n,
200	                     "precision": prec, "recall": rec, "f1": f1})
201	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)
202

204	def compare_to_static(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
205	    """Per (strategy, classifier, year): F1 and accuracy minus the static model of the same classifier."""
206	    static = results[results["strategy"] == "static"].set_index(["classifier", "year"])
207	    out = results[["strategy", "classifier", "year", "f1", "accuracy"]].copy()
208	    key = list(zip(out["classifier"], out["year"]))
209	    out["f1_static"] = [static["f1"].get(k, np.nan) for k in key]
210	    out["accuracy_static"] = [static["accuracy"].get(k, np.nan) for k in key]
211	    out["f1_diff"] = out["f1"] - out["f1_static"]
212	    out["accuracy_diff"] = out["accuracy"] - out["accuracy_static"]
213	    return out[out["strategy"] != "static"].reset_index(drop=True)
214	
215	
216	def summary_table(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
217	    """Per (strategy, classifier): mean F1 over the 5 test years (unweighted), worst year, 2019-2021 means, gain over static."""
218	    rows = []
219	    for (strategy, clf), g in results.groupby(["strategy", "classifier"], sort=False):
220	        worst = g.loc[g["f1"].idxmin()]
221	        late = g[g["year"] >= 2019]
222	        rows.append({"strategy": strategy, "classifier": clf, "mean_f1": g["f1"].mean(), "worst_f1": worst["f1"],
223	                     "worst_year": int(worst["year"]), "mean_f1_2019_21": late["f1"].mean(),
224	                     "mean_accuracy_2019_21": late["accuracy"].mean(), "mean_accuracy": g["accuracy"].mean()})
225	    out = pd.DataFrame(rows)
226	    base = out[out["strategy"] == "static"].set_index("classifier")
227	    out["mean_f1_gain_vs_static"] = out["mean_f1"] - out["classifier"].map(base["mean_f1"])
228	    out["mean_acc_2019_21_gain_vs_static"] = out["mean_accuracy_2019_21"] - out["classifier"].map(base["mean_accuracy_2019_21"])
229	    return out

232	def cost_table(results: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
233	    """Training cost per (strategy, classifier): number of fits/updates, total and mean seconds, mean training rows."""
234	    rows = []
235	    for (strategy, clf), g in results.groupby(["strategy", "classifier"], sort=False):
236	        if strategy == "static":
237	            secs = g["train_seconds"].iloc[:1]  # one fit, paid once
238	        else:
239	            secs = g["train_seconds"]
240	        rows.append({"strategy": strategy, "classifier": clf, "n_fits": len(secs), "total_seconds": secs.sum(),
241	                     "mean_seconds_per_update": secs.mean(), "max_seconds": secs.max(),
242	                     "mean_train_rows": g["train_rows"].mean()})
243	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

246	def window_composition(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
247	    """Rows per year in the training data behind each prediction, for every strategy and test year.
248	
249	    The incremental model has seen the same years as the expanding window (2014..t-1) but through the single
250	    pass of `partial_fit`; its preprocessor only ever saw 2014-2016.
251	    """
252	    counts = df.groupby(YEAR_COL).size()
253	    rows = []
254	    for strategy in STRATEGIES:
255	        for t in TEST_YEARS:
256	            years = window_years("expanding" if strategy == "incremental" else strategy, t)
257	            total = int(sum(counts[y] for y in years))
258	            row = {"strategy": strategy, "test_year": t, "window": f"{min(years)}-{max(years)}", "train_rows": total}
259	            row.update({f"n_{y}": int(counts[y]) if y in years else 0 for y in sorted(counts.index)})
260	            row["share_2014_2018"] = sum(int(counts[y]) for y in years if y <= 2018) / total
261	            row["share_last_year"] = int(counts[max(years)]) / total
262	            rows.append(row)
263	    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

266	def plot_strategies(results: pd.DataFrame, path: Path) -> None:
267	    """Save F1 (top) and accuracy (bottom) by test year, one panel per classifier, one line per strategy.
268	
269	    Dashed lines: F1 of always predicting malware on a balanced year (2*0.5/(0.5+1) = 0.667) and accuracy 0.5.
270	    """
271	    import matplotlib
272	
273	    matplotlib.use("Agg")
274	    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
275	
276	    clfs = list(dict.fromkeys(results["classifier"]))
277	    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, len(clfs), figsize=(4.5 * len(clfs), 7), sharex=True, squeeze=False)
278	    for j, clf in enumerate(clfs):
279	        for i, (metric, chance, label) in enumerate((("f1", 2 / 3, "always-malware F1 = 0.667"), ("accuracy", 0.5, "chance accuracy = 0.5"))):
280	            ax = axes[i][j]
281	            for strategy, g in results[results["classifier"] == clf].groupby("strategy", sort=False):
282	                g = g.sort_values("year")
283	                ax.plot(g["year"], g[metric], marker="o", label=strategy)
284	            ax.axhline(chance, ls="--", color="gray", label=label)
285	            ax.set_title(f"{clf}: {metric} by test year")
286	            ax.set_xticks(list(TEST_YEARS))
287	            ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
288	            ax.legend(fontsize=7)
289	            if j == 0:
290	                ax.set_ylabel(f"{metric} (malware = positive class)")
291	        axes[1][j].set_xlabel("test year")
292	    fig.tight_layout()
293	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
294	    fig.savefig(path, dpi=120)
295	    plt.close(fig)
296

298	def run_sustainable(
299	    df: pd.DataFrame,
300	    split: dict | None = None,
301	    models: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
302	    step4_seconds: dict[str, float] | None = None,
303	    rf: bool = True,
304	) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
305	    """Run all strategies, write results/step7_* (strategies, pooled, vs_static, summary, cost, window_composition, png)."""
306	    results = run_all_strategies(df, split, models, step4_seconds, rf)
307	    tables = {
308	        "strategies": results,
309	        "pooled": pooled_by_strategy(results),
310	        "vs_static": compare_to_static(results),
311	        "summary": summary_table(results),
312	        "cost": cost_table(results),
313	        "window_composition": window_composition(df),
314	    }
315	    save_table(results[EXPORT_COLUMNS], "step7_strategies")
316	    save_table(results, "step7_strategies_detail")  # + confusion counts, cost, window
317	    for name in ("pooled", "vs_static", "summary", "cost", "window_composition"):
318	        save_table(tables[name], f"step7_{name}")
319	    plot_strategies(results, RESULTS_DIR / "step7_f1_by_year.png")
320	    return tables

content.text:
Written for: the student reviewing Step 7 test coverage.

I wrote 33 test functions in `tests/test_step7_sustainable.py`. They expand to 66 cases, and all 66 passed in one run of `python harness.py test 7` (27 s). I committed them with `tests/step7_test_log.md` as `eb5fb66`. I didn't change anything in `src/`.

Two of my own tests failed during development, and both were my mistakes, not the code's. One reused object ids in my recording stub, and one miscounted the expected rows (35, not 30). Both are fixed. They aren't in the log's failures table because no failure survived to the logged run.

**What the tests cover**
- **No future training years:**
  - Recording stubs log every `fit`, `partial_fit` and `predict`. Replaying the log shows no model, for any strategy or classifier including random forest, was trained on a year at or after the year it predicts.
  - The preprocessor and scaler are fit on the same years as the model, never on year t.
  - A second check with real models flips the 2019 labels. Predictions for 2019 and earlier don't change, and the static baseline doesn't change at any year.
- **Windows:**
  - Expanding is exactly 2014 to t-1 and sliding is exactly the 3 years before t.
  - The window helper raises on an empty or invalid year.
  - The fit log matches the planned windows in order.
- **Incremental:** The call order is `fit` on 2014-2016, then `predict(t)` followed by `partial_fit(t)` for each year from 2017 to 2021. It uses one model object, and its preprocessor is fit once on 2014-2016.
- **Updated model uses newer data:**
  - With real logreg, the expanding and sliding coefficients change each year, and the expanding window grows by one year of rows each time.
  - With real SGD, `partial_fit` is called once per test year and the coefficients change.
- **Static baseline never updated:**
  - The Step 4 coefficients are identical before and after `main.run_step7`.
  - Stub static models that raise on `fit` or `partial_fit` still produce static rows.
  - Static rows match sklearn's metrics on the same rows.
- **Results:**
  - One row per strategy, classifier and year, with every strategy scored on the same test rows.
  - Metrics are between 0 and 1.
  - The pooled, comparison, window-composition and output-file checks pass.
- **Edge cases:** A single-class test year doesn't crash. A missing year doesn't produce a made-up row. Missing training years raise.
- **Real data:** One test checks the window years against the real file names and is skipped when `input_data/` is empty. I didn't run the random forest on the full data.

**Sources and judgment calls**
- **Row counts:** I followed AGENTS.md (18,000 rows per year for 2014-2018 and 3,000 for 2019-2021). The synthetic tests use small frames, so this only matters for the real-data test.
- **Strategy set:** I followed PLAN.md. Logreg gets static, expanding and sliding. SGD also gets incremental. Random forest gets static and expanding only. That's 45 rows in total.
- **Synthetic drift:** I built it in my own helper. The signal moves from one feature to another across the years.
- **Missing 2019 test:** The test passes whether the code raises or just omits 2019. Either is acceptable under the lead engineer's note.

**Issues for the lead engineer:** None. The two plan-vs-code points I noticed, the cost table and the static fit being shared across years, are outside what the tests assert.
